 * Asking a resolved binary what it thinks it is.
 *
 * Resolution tells you which file wins. It does not tell you that the file is
 * a two-year-old release, or that the winner and the shadowed copy behind it
 * are different major versions of the same tool. That gap is the whole reason
 * a `--version` in one shell disagrees with a `--version` in another.
 *
 * Running a binary is not free, so the rules are narrow: only files that
 * resolution already picked, only a known-safe version flag, a short timeout,
 * and a bounded amount of output. Nothing here is a general command runner.
 *
 * @module dsh-which/lib/probe
 */

import { execFile } from 'node:child_process'
import { promisify } from 'node:util'

const run = promisify(execFile)

/** Flags that ask a program for its version and exit. */
export const VERSION_FLAGS = ['--version', '-v', 'version', '-V']

/** How long a probe may take before it is abandoned. */
export const DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 4000

/** Output cap per probe, so a chatty program cannot flood the result. */
const MAX_OUTPUT = 8 * 1024

/**
 * Pull the most version-looking line out of a program's output.
 *
 * Programs are inconsistent: some print a bare number, some a banner, some put
 * the version on stderr. A line containing a digit and a dot is the best
 * available signal, and the first such line is almost always the version.
 *
 * @param {string} text - combined output.
 * @returns {string | undefined} the version line, when one is recognisable.
 */
export function extractVersion(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') return undefined
  const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/u).map((line) => line.trim()).filter((line) => line !== '')
  for (const line of lines) {
    if (/\d+\.\d+/u.test(line)) return line
  }
  return lines.length > 0 ? lines[0] : undefined
}

/**
 * Run one program with a version flag.
 *
 * A probe never throws: a program that hangs, exits non-zero, or does not
 * understand the flag is a result, not an error. The only thing worth
 * distinguishing is "we learned its version" from "we did not", and why.
 *
 * @param {string} file - absolute path to the program.
 * @param {{
 *   flag?: string,
 *   timeoutMs?: number,
 *   signal?: AbortSignal,
 *   platform?: string,
 *   run?: typeof run,
 * }} [options] - probe inputs.
 * @returns {Promise<{ path: string, flag: string, ok: boolean, version?: string, exitCode?: number, reason?: string, output?: string }>} the probe result.
 */
export async function probeVersion(file, options = {}) {
  const flag = options.flag ?? VERSION_FLAGS[0]
  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS
  const platform = options.platform ?? process.platform
  const runner = options.run ?? run

  try {
    const { stdout, stderr } = await runner(file, [flag], {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      maxBuffer: MAX_OUTPUT,
      windowsHide: true,
      ...(options.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: options.signal }),
    })
    const combined = `${stdout ?? ''}${stderr ?? ''}`
    const version = extractVersion(combined)
    return version === undefined
      ? { path: file, flag, ok: false, reason: 'ran, but printed nothing that looks like a version' }
      : { path: file, flag, ok: true, version }
  } catch (error) {
    return { path: file, flag, ok: false, ...describeFailure(error, platform) }
  }
}

/**
 * Turn a failed probe into a reason a person can act on.
 *
 * @param {unknown} error - the thrown error.
 * @param {string} platform - platform.
 * @returns {{ reason: string, exitCode?: number, output?: string }} the description.
 */
function describeFailure(error, platform) {
  const code = error?.code
  const killed = error?.killed === true
  const timedOut = error?.signal === 'SIGTERM' && killed

  if (timedOut || code === 'ETIMEDOUT') {
    return { reason: 'did not answer in time' }
  }
  if (code === 'ENOENT') {
    return { reason: 'no such file' }
  }
  if (code === 'EACCES' || code === 'EPERM') {
    return { reason: 'not permitted to run it' }
  }

  /* A program that prints its version and exits non-zero is common enough
   * (`java -version` does it) that its output still counts. */
  const stdout = typeof error?.stdout === 'string' ? error.stdout : ''
  const stderr = typeof error?.stderr === 'string' ? error.stderr : ''
  const output = `${stdout}${stderr}`
  const version = extractVersion(output)
  const numeric = typeof code === 'number' ? code : Number.parseInt(String(code ?? ''), 10)
  const exitCode = Number.isFinite(numeric) ? numeric : undefined

  if (version !== undefined && output.trim() !== '') {
    return { reason: `exited non-zero but printed a version`, exitCode, output: version }
  }
  if (exitCode !== undefined) {
    return { reason: `exited with status ${exitCode}`, exitCode }
  }
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
  return { reason: platform === 'win32' ? `could not run it: ${message}` : `could not run it: ${message}` }
}

/**
 * Probe the winner of a resolution and, optionally, everything behind it.
 *
 * The comparison is the point: two files answering to one name and reporting
 * different versions is the concrete form of "my terminal and my agent are
 * running different tools".
 *
 * @param {{ winner: object | null, candidates: object[] }} resolution - a resolution.
 * @param {{
 *   includeShadowed?: boolean,
 *   flag?: string,
 *   timeoutMs?: number,
 *   signal?: AbortSignal,
 *   platform?: string,
 *   run?: typeof run,
 * } } [options] - probe options.
 * @returns {Promise<{ winner: object | null, shadowed: object[], divergent: boolean }>} probe outcome.
 */
export async function probeResolution(resolution, options = {}) {
  const shared = {
    flag: options.flag,
    timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs,
    signal: options.signal,
    platform: options.platform,
    run: options.run,
  }

  const winner = resolution.winner === null ? null : await probeVersion(resolution.winner.path, shared)

  const shadowed = []
  if (options.includeShadowed === true) {
    for (const candidate of resolution.candidates) {
      if (candidate.path === resolution.winner?.path) continue
      shadowed.push({ candidate, probe: await probeVersion(candidate.path, shared) })
    }
  }

  const versions = new Set()
  if (winner?.ok === true) versions.add(winner.version)
  for (const entry of shadowed) {
    if (entry.probe.ok === true) versions.add(entry.probe.version)
  }

  return { winner, shadowed, divergent: versions.size > 1 }
}

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "# dsh-web-restart

One-click restart button for the **DeepSeek Harness Web UI**.

Adds a small circular restart button (↻) to the sidebar footer, next to Settings. A **single click** immediately restarts the `dsh web` process — the page disconnects for ~15–20 seconds, then you refresh and everything is back (sessions are persisted on disk and recover automatically). The button is **persistent**: it survives the restart it triggers.

> Windows-specific: the restart launches `dsh web` through an independent hidden PowerShell process, so the script keeps running after the harness process is killed.

## Features

- Single-click restart — no confirmation step, no double-click dance.
- Persistent: survives the DSH restart it triggers (installed as a bundle-layer plugin, not a dynamic session plugin).
- Small footprint: sits beside the Settings trigger in the sidebar footer; icon-only in the 56px rail, icon + label in the wide sidebar.
- In-flight feedback: the button turns red and shows "重启中…" → "已触发" while the request is being processed.
- Re-entry guard: a second click while a restart is already in flight is rejected.
- Online status dot: the button also shows DSH liveness — a green dot polls `GET /dsh-health` every 5s (red when the harness is unreachable/restarting).

## Install

### From GitHub (this repo)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:YOUR_OWNER/dsh-web-restart
```

Then restart `dsh web` once so the bundle layer loads.

### Manual (edit profile files)

1. Add the dependency:

```jsonc
// ~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-web-restart": "github:YOUR_OWNER/dsh-web-restart"
  }
}
```

2. Add the plugin row (this repo ships its own `cordis.patch.yml` — either merge its row into your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or install via the `dsh plugin` command above which does it for you):

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-web-restart
      name: dsh-web-restart
```

3. `pnpm install` in the profile directory, then restart `dsh web`.

## How it works

| Layer | File | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host | `lib/index.js` | Registers an exact `POST /restart-dsh` route on the webServer; launches the restart script as an independent hidden PowerShell under `danger-full-access` sandbox policy |
| Client | `lib/client.js` | Registers the sidebar footer button (slot `sidebar.footer.action`); single click `fetch`es `POST /restart-dsh`; polls `GET /dsh-health` every 5s for the status dot |
| Bundle | `cordis.patch.yml` | The loader row that mounts both halves |

The host routes return **before** the restart happens (~1s host timer + 3s inner sleep), giving the browser time to render the "restarting" state before the page drops.

### Why not `ctx.timeout` in the route handler

`ctx.timeout` is a Cordis mixin backed by `ctx.effect()`, which is scoped to the Cordis **fiber** lifecycle. A `webServer` route handler runs as a plain Node HTTP callback — outside any fiber — so `ctx.effect`-registered timers are silently dropped and the restart never fires. This plugin uses Node's native `setTimeout` in the handler instead.

## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness `0.1.0-rc.6` (web profile).
- The restart script path (`D:\1\dsh-web-host.ps1`) is hard-coded for this author's machine — **fork and adjust it** (or replace the command in `lib/index.js`) for your own environment. Contributions to make this configurable are welcome.

## Development

The client bundle is hand-written in the exact wire format (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`), so no build step is required:

```bash
node --check lib/index.js
node --check lib/client.js
```

## License

MIT

      "path": "lib/index.js",
      "content": "/**
 * dsh-web-restart — host half.
 *
 * Registers an exact POST route `/restart-dsh` on the webServer. The client
 * button (lib/client.js) fetches this route; the handler launches the dsh web
 * restart script as an independent hidden PowerShell process (Start-Process
 * wrapper so the script survives the DSH kill), under danger-full-access so
 * netstat/Stop-Process are not sandbox-denied.
 *
 * Also registers GET /dsh-health — a lightweight liveness probe the client
 * status dot polls every few seconds.
 *
 * The route returns BEFORE the restart happens (1s timer + 3s inner sleep),
 * so the browser has time to render the "restarting" state before the page
 * drops.
 */
export const name = 'dsh-web-restart'
export const inject = ['webServer', 'shell']

export function apply(ctx) {
  let restarting = false

  const disposeHealth = ctx.webServer.register({
    kind: 'exact',
    path: '/dsh-health',
    handler: async (req, res) => {
      res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'cache-control': 'no-store' })
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, ts: Date.now() }))
    }
  })

  const disposeRoute = ctx.webServer.register({
    kind: 'exact',
    path: '/restart-dsh',
    handler: async (req, res) => {
      if (req.method !== 'POST') {
        res.writeHead(405, { 'content-type': 'application/json' })
        res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: false, message: 'method not allowed' }))
        return
      }
      if (restarting) {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json' })
        res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: false, message: '重启已在进行中，请稍候' }))
        return
      }
      restarting = true
      // 注意：webServer handler 是纯 Node http 回调，不在 Cordis fiber 上下文里，
      // ctx.timeout（mixin→ctx.effect）在此不触发；改用 Node 原生 setTimeout。
      setTimeout(() => {
        try {
          // 独立进程 + 内部 3 秒延迟：DSH 被脚本杀掉后脚本继续执行，前端有时间渲染状态
          const command = "Start-Process powershell -ArgumentList '-NoProfile','-ExecutionPolicy','Bypass','-Command','Start-Sleep -Seconds 3; & \"D:\\1\\dsh-web-host.ps1\"' -WindowStyle Hidden"
          const spec = ctx.shell.resolve({
            command,
            sandboxPolicy: { mode: 'danger-full-access' }
          })
          ctx.shell.start(spec)
          console.log('[dsh-web-restart] restart script launched')
        } catch (error) {
          restarting = false
          console.error('[dsh-web-restart] failed to launch restart:', error)
        }
      }, 1000)
      res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json' })
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, message: '重启已触发：DSH 将断开约 15-20 秒，之后请刷新页面' }))
    }
  })

  return () => { disposeHealth(); disposeRoute() }
}

# 蓝毛小女仆 · Blue-Haired Little Maid **A free, open-source desktop pet for Windows: a transparent little maid who lives on your desktop.** She idles, wanders around and does little animations on her own. She can chat with you, take a look at your screen and say something about it — and when you ask her to, she can open an app, a file, a folder or a web page for you, or start a screen recording. ![She has 106 hand-drawn animations](docs/images/demo.gif) [Install](#install) · [First run](#what-she-does-on-first-run) · [Data & privacy](#data--privacy) · [Build from source](#build-from-source) · [Verify your download](#verify-your-download) · [License](#license--third-party) **English** · [中文文档](README.zh-CN.md)
--- ## About this project **蓝毛小女仆 (Blue-Haired Little Maid)** is an independent desktop-pet project, developed and maintained by **Mikolu**. Special thanks to **PC2005-cloud**, whose **dsh-pet 0.3.0** provided the early foundation and the inspiration for this project. The pet engine in [`src/`](src) is that codebase, carried forward and maintained in-tree: of the 243 files in the published upstream `dsh-pet@0.3.0` package, **232 are byte-identical here and 11 were changed on purpose** (each one listed with sizes and reasons in [docs/differences-from-upstream.md](docs/differences-from-upstream.md)), **no upstream file was dropped**, and three engine files (`runtime/electron-helper/obs-ctl.js`, `stt-worker.mjs`, `targets.js`) are ours. Everything else in this repository — the console, the standalone runner, the build chain, the installer, the docs — is this project's own work. There is no patching step any more: `src/` **is** the shipped source. Building is just laying the source tree out in release shape and adding the runtimes that are not kept in git. | | | | --- | --- | | Product name | **蓝毛小女仆** (Blue-Haired Little Maid) | | Repository / package / installer name | `cute-fat-fish-pet` — legacy display name "Cute Fat Fish Pet" / 「可爱大肥鱼桌宠」 | | Author / maintainer | Mikolu | | Version | 1.2.3 | | License | MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) | > **On the name.** 蓝毛小女仆 is the product's name. The repository and the npm package keep the bare identifier **`cute-fat-fish-pet`**, and the installers shipped so far still carry the older display name **Cute Fat Fish Pet** / 「可爱大肥鱼桌宠」 — renaming those would break existing installs, shortcuts and download links, so they stay as they are. Until the next repack, Windows still shows 「可爱大肥鱼桌宠」 on the desktop shortcut and in *Settings → Apps*. ### Internal identifiers are kept on purpose (`BlueHairMaid`) Everything the user can see has been renamed, and so has the **DSH plugin package name** (it collided with the upstream npm package). Everything else on the inside has not — on purpose: | Internal identifier | Value | What breaks if it is renamed | | --- | --- | --- | | App folder / APP_ID / uninstall entry | `BlueHairMaid` | Existing config, data, shortcuts and "Apps & features" entry no longer match — it becomes a second pet | | Pet plugin package name *(renamed 2026-10-10)* | `dsh-pet` → `cute-fat-fish-pet` | Nothing user-visible: the data root and route prefix below are hard-coded strings in `src/lib/`, not derived from the package name, so persona and memory stay put. An already-installed copy just has to be re-added once. | | Desktop renderer package | `dsh-pet-electron-helper` | The pet page's localStorage (position, size, sprite state) is lost and she is put back in the middle of the screen | | Browser storage keys | `dsh-pet-*` | Same as above — all existing settings are ignored | | Local route prefix | `/dsh-pet-7340` | Incompatible with the already-shipped versions; console and pet stop understanding each other | | User data directory | `%APPDATA%\BlueHairMaid` | Existing persona / memory / screen-watch state is lost | In short: **rename what is visible — plus the plugin package name, once — but never touch the identifiers that hold user data.** That is what makes upgrading from 1.0.0 a no-op for the user. The same list is in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) (section 5), and the reasoning behind it is in [docs/architecture-roadmap.zh-CN.md](docs/architecture-roadmap.zh-CN.md). --- ## What she can do ![The console](docs/images/console.png) - **She moves on her own** — 106 hand-drawn transparent animations (VP9-alpha webm, composited onto your wallpaper with a screen blend). Idle breathing, looking around, walking to random spots, random small gestures. Animation weights and frequency are configurable. - **She talks with you** — click her to open the chat. Local models through [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the console has three modes: **Local**, **Auto (best available)** and **Online**. - **She can watch your screen** (optional, switchable) — a screenshot every so often is handed to a vision model and she comments on it. With no vision model configured this path stays off instead of sending a random image. - **She mutters and speaks up** — she fills quiet moments on her own, and can be driven by work state (task started / finished / failed). - **She can do things for you (your call)** — open an app, a file, a folder or a URL; screen recording goes to OBS or to whatever software you pick, saved wherever you pick. Three permission switches turn this off completely. - **Voice** — speech input runs fully offline inside the package (sherpa-onnx + SenseVoice int8); her voice uses Edge TTS + SSML, with adjustable rate and pitch (the pitch is stored in the data root). - **One single-HTML console** — start / stop, status, models and "AI brain", voice, permissions, recording, logs: all in one window, no command line. - **Persona and memory** — persona files, chat history and screen-watch state live in the data root; you can edit them and back the whole thing up. ![Right-click menu](docs/images/menu.png) --- ## Install ### Option 1 — installer (recommended) Download **`cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-setup.exe`** (about 331.8 MB, NSIS) and double-click it. > **Always-latest link:** every release also carries a byte-identical copy without the version in > its name, so this one link always points at the newest installer: > - Installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BlueHairMaid` by default — **no administrator rights needed**. - Want it elsewhere (D: drive, external disk)? Change it on the "Choose install location" page. Start-menu entry and desktop shortcut are created for you. - The package already contains the Electron runtime, the speech engine and models, and the real `node.exe` used for speech recognition, so it works **offline** right after installing. ![Installer](docs/images/installer.png) ### Option 2 — portable zip Download **`cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-win-x64.zip`** (about 397.7 MB, ~760 MB unpacked), unpack it anywhere, then pick one: > **1.1.1 fixed this path end to end.** Unpack the zip **first** (right-click → *Extract All…*) and only then double-click > `安装.cmd` inside the extracted folder. It checks that the package is complete and explains the problem in Chinese if it > is not (the old one just flashed and closed), installs under the name 「可爱大肥鱼桌宠」 with the real version number, and > `卸载.cmd` now really removes the directory instead of leaving all 714 files behind. > Details: [release notes 1.2.2](docs/release-notes-1.2.2.md) · [confirmed defects](docs/known-issues.md). - double-click `安装.cmd` — creates the shortcuts and the uninstall entry (as if it had been installed), or - double-click `standalone\start-pet.vbs` to start her and `standalone\stop-pet.vbs` to stop her (fully portable, writes no registry keys). Use the second one on a USB stick. If you want her data to travel with the program directory, drop an empty `portable.txt` next to the executable (see [Data & privacy](#data--privacy)). > Note: the files that ship **inside** the package keep their Chinese names and Chinese text for now (`安装.cmd`, `卸载.cmd`, `assets\使用说明.txt`, …). Renaming them would change the package that is already published, so it is queued for the next release instead. ### Option 3 — as a DeepSeek Harness plugin (no installer) The pet engine in [`src/`](src) is also a **DeepSeek Harness** plugin, so she can live inside the DSH Web UI instead of on your wallpaper: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:12we21/cute-fat-fish-pet#path:/src ``` > **What that downloads.** The manifest lives in the `src/` subpackage, so this fetches the **whole repository tarball (about 68 MB)** — the 106 animations are most of it. On a slow or throttled connection that fetch can time out. If it does, install from a local clone instead: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/12we21/cute-fat-fish-pet dsh plugin --profile web add ./cute-fat-fish-pet/src ``` `src/lib/` is committed pre-built, so there is no build step. The repository carries the `dsh-plugin` topic and has been submitted to the [Awesome DSH Plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) directory under *Just for Fun* — that directory is what `dshmarket` and `awesome-dsh-plugin.com` read, while [dshfind](https://dshfind.com) mirrors every repository carrying the topic. This half of the project is a **subset** of the standalone build: all 106 animations, wandering, click reactions, chat through local **Ollama** or the DSH online models, and optional screen watching are in it. The offline speech recognition, the Edge TTS voice and the console window are **not** — those come with the installer and the zip above. ### Every download comes with a `.sha256` `cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-setup.exe.sha256` and `cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-win-x64.zip.sha256`, in the format ` `: ```powershell Get-FileHash .\cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 ``` > Release file names are ASCII on purpose: GitHub Releases deletes non-ASCII characters from > asset names (a Chinese name is uploaded as `-1.1.0-.exe`). Chinese stays in the product name, > the shortcuts and "Apps & features". ### Start, stop, uninstall - **Start**: double-click the desktop shortcut "可爱大肥鱼桌宠" to open the **console**, then press **启动桌宠** ("Start the pet"). The console does **not** pull her up by itself — that is deliberate, so that changing a setting does not make her pop out first. - **Stop**: press stop in the console, or double-click `standalone\stop-pet.vbs`. - **Autostart and auto-update are not implemented yet.** If you want autostart, put a shortcut to the console into your Startup folder. - **Uninstall**: "可爱大肥鱼桌宠" in Settings → Apps, or `卸载.cmd` in the install directory. Uninstalling **does not** delete your data (persona, memory, chat history stay). To remove everything, delete the data directory yourself (next section). ### Updating to a newer version There is **no automatic updater yet** — updating means downloading the new installer and running it over the old copy. Only program files are replaced; your data is not touched. 1. **Close the pet first.** Right-click her tray icon → exit, or double-click `standalone\stop-pet.vbs`. The installer deliberately never kills processes (it must not kill a *different* pet on the same PC), so while `electron.exe` is running it stops and asks you to close her. 2. **Download the new installer** — the always-latest link above, or the newest release on the [releases page](https://github.com/12we21/cute-fat-fish-pet/releases). 3. **Double-click it and click Next.** The installer reads the folder used by the previous version from `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\BlueHairMaid` and installs **back into the same folder**, so you do not end up with a second 761 MB copy. The desktop and Start-menu shortcuts are recreated. 4. **Start her again** from the console. What survives: persona, memory, chat history, settings and model configuration live in the data directory (`%APPDATA%\BlueHairMaid`), which the installer never touches. Portable zip: unpack the new zip over the old folder. Keep your own `standalone\online.json` (your online-model settings) and your `portable.txt` if you made one. > Scripted installs: `cute-fat-fish-pet-setup.exe /S /D=D:\path\to\install`. Two things to know — silent mode does **not** auto-detect the previous folder, so pass `/D=` yourself, and it will not replace files while she is running. --- ## What she does on first run You do not have to configure anything. On the first start she does a "local fit" round: 1. **Looks at your GPU** — reads the VRAM size from the registry to decide the model context size and when to unload it (the result is written to `device-profile.json`). 2. **Finds local models** — lists the models already pulled into Ollama and picks one as the chat model, plus a vision model for screen watching if there is one. 3. **Seeds the defaults** — copies the bundled default persona / animation config / screen-watch config into the data root. **Only missing files are added; files you edited are never overwritten.** 4. **Writes a run record** — `runtime.json` (pid, port, model, start time), removed on exit; it is the first place to look when she does not come up. She also runs with **no model at all**: she will idle, wander and gesture, she just will not speak. To give her a voice, install [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) and pull a model, or fill in an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (base URL + key + model name) under **模型 · AI 大脑 → 联网模型** in the console. --- ## Data & privacy ### Where the data lives Treat the program directory (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\BlueHairMaid`) as **read-only**. Everything that changes lives in the user data directory, resolved in this order: 1. environment variable `DSH_PET_DATA_DIR` (testing / advanced use) 2. `data-root.txt` in the program directory (one line: the path) 3. `portable.txt` in the program directory → data goes to `\userdata\` (portable mode) 4. **default** `%APPDATA%\BlueHairMaid\` ``` %APPDATA%\BlueHairMaid\ ├─ dsh-pet\ │ ├─ main-config.json persona + pet list │ ├─ screen-watch\state.json screen-watch config and state, brain mode, local models │ ├─ record.json recording settings (which app, where to save) │ ├─ tts-pitch.txt voice pitch (default +0Hz) │ └─ main-animation\ your own animation assets (used with priority if present) ├─ device-profile.json result of the automatic first-run fit ├─ runtime.json run record (pid / port / model), deleted on exit ├─ console\ console window state └─ logs\ ├─ runner.log / runner.err.log host-side logs └─ pet-control.log console start/stop log ``` The pet page's own localStorage (position, size, sprite state) lives in `%APPDATA%\dsh-pet-electron-helper` — that is Electron's rule, which is why it is part of the "internal identifiers are kept" note above. ### Data root when installed as a DSH plugin Installed through the DSH plugin route (`dsh plugin --profile web add github:12we21/cute-fat-fish-pet`), she does not use `%APPDATA%\BlueHairMaid`. The host half resolves the DSH home and keeps everything under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/`: ``` $DSH_HOME\ └─ dsh-pet\ ├─ main-config.json persona + pet list (the user layer over the bundled defaults) ├─ memory.json chat memory; the host process is its only writer ├─ pet\ per-pet config files └─ main-animation\ your own animation assets for the browser half ``` `$DSH_HOME` is DSH's own home directory (`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` by default). Two things worth knowing about coexistence: - This is **not** `$DSH_HOME/pets\`. That directory belongs to the market's v2 pet *asset* packs (`petManifestVersion: 2` plus `pet.json`), which ship content only. This plugin is a cordis bundle with its own host half and browser half, so the two never read or write each other's directory. - The upstream plugin (`@linxin666/dsh-pet`) uses the **same** `$DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/` root. Install one of the two, not both: they would share `main-config.json` and `memory.json`. ### Privacy - **Screen watching** is **a local screenshot handed to the model you chose**. Pick a local Ollama model and nothing leaves your machine; pick an online model and the image goes to the endpoint you configured. Turn it off in the console and no screenshot is taken at all. - **Speech recognition runs offline**: sherpa-onnx + SenseVoice int8 are inside the package and need no network. - **Edge TTS needs the network** (it uses Microsoft's online speech synthesis). - **Online model API keys are stored in plain text** in `standalone\online.json` (in the program directory). It is a local file meant for you only — do not send this file to anyone, and do not upload a directory that contains it. - **She never phones home**: no telemetry, no usage reporting. Build from source **Requirements**: Windows x64, Node.js 24, Python 3 (packaging scripts), [NSIS 3](https://nsis.sourceforge.io/) (to build the installer). **The three runtime pieces (~689 MB) are not in git** and have to come from somewhere: | Piece | What it is | Size | | --- | --- | --- | | `electron\` | Electron 43.3.0 win-x64 | ~347 MB | | `node\` | node v24.21.0 win-x64 (the SenseVoice native addon cannot be loaded inside Electron: `External buffers are not allowed`, so a real node.exe is required) | ~89 MB | | `speech\` | sherpa-onnx native engine + SenseVoice int8 model | ~253 MB | The easy way is to point the build at **an already installed copy of Cute Fat Fish Pet**, which has all three: ```powershell npm run toolchain # show what is missing and where to get it node build\build.mjs --toolchain # lay out stage\ npm run exe # python build\mkexe.py → release\cute-fat-fish-pet--setup.exe npm run zip # python build\mkzip.py → release\cute-fat-fish-pet--win-x64.zip npm run verify # check the stage\ tree fingerprints (should be all OK) npm run paths # build-time privacy gate: no local absolute paths, no private dirs ``` The two commands used most while developing: ```powershell node build\build.mjs launcher assets # rebuild only these blocks node build\build.mjs --list # show what it would do, touch nothing ``` Blocks: `app launcher standalone defaults assets verify electron node speech`. Artifact names come from the `version` field in `src\package.json` and are ASCII-only (GitHub Releases drops non-ASCII asset names), so this version produces `cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-setup.exe` and `cute-fat-fish-pet-1.2.3-win-x64.zip`. > The build contract lives in the header of `build\build.mjs` and in the root `package.json` scripts. > `build\check-paths.mjs` is a build gate; `--no-gate` skips it (not recommended). --- ## Tech stack - **Desktop rendering** — one transparent, borderless Electron 43 window per pet; plain JS + Canvas playing VP9-alpha webm, screen-blended onto the wallpaper. The window follows the pet's bounding box and is click-through by default, becoming interactive only when the cursor is inside her body. - **Host side** — one file, [`src\lib\index.js`](src/lib/index.js), lives two lives: inside DSH it is a Cordis plugin (`name/inject/apply`); in standalone mode `standalone\main.mjs` redirects three `@deepseek-ai/*` packages to `standalone\shims\` at run time, feeds it a "just enough" fake ctx (`standalone\context.mjs`) and calls the very same `apply(ctx)`. - **Console** — a single HTML file (`launcher\index.html`) plus an Electron shell, IPC into `pet-api.js`; start/stop goes through `standalone\main.mjs` / `stop-pet.mjs`. - **Models** — local Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/chat/completions`, vision through `image_url`); balance lookup uses DeepSeek's `/user/balance`. - **Speech** — sherpa-onnx + SenseVoice int8 + silero VAD for offline recognition; Edge TTS + SSML for synthesis. - **Console ↔ pet channel** — a loopback control bridge, hardened in 1.1.0 with token auth and a CORS allow-list (see the [release notes](docs/release-notes-1.1.0.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)). - **Packaging** — Node + Python scripts lay out `stage\`; data/runs/2026-10-20-04/snapshots/101567.content: { "repository": "1015677515/dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk", "revision": "fab9373ac396e430316b09693b654051583e9713", "component": "", "inspected_paths": [ "index.js", "client.js", "CHANGELOG.md" ], "files": [ { "path": "README.md", "content": "# dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk > 本项目由 DeepSeek Harness 的 AI 智能体独立开发。 对话标题栏里的两个小面板：编辑提示词、维护错误经验库。 [English](#english) | 中文 --- ## 它做什么 | 面板 | 作用 | |---|---| | **提示词** | 编辑**跨对话**的全局提示词，以及**本次对话**的提示词（新对话会延续）。面板顶部显示哪一半当前正在生效。 | | **错误库** | **按分类**归纳反复犯的错误：每条一个简短类型 + 一句教训，归入三档分类之一。**最近 10 条（条数可自己设）会被注入系统提示词**，让后续对话以极低的 token 成本吸取教训。agent 按格式汇报「我犯了个错误：错误经过：… 教训：…」时会被自动捕获成待确认草稿。 | 第二个面板的意义：一个反复犯同类错误的 agent，会在自己的上下文里收到一份简短的、按分类归好的提醒，成本远低于重新踩一遍坑再发现。 **点面板以外的空白处会自动关闭**（按 Esc 也可以）。 ## 界面预览 **错误经验库** —— 按分类折叠，每条带下拉框可改类；顶部显示注入条数，底部是自动捕获的待确认草稿： ![错误经验库面板](picture/errornotes.png) **提示词** —— 顶部自检状态与「临时暂停注入」，中间是全局与本次对话提示词，底部是实际注入文本的预览（可拖拽调高，也可隐藏；三个框都能竖向拖动）： ![提示词面板](picture/prompt.png) ## 安装 本插件目前只发布在 GitHub（未发布到 npm）。 > 完整的安装步骤、验证方法与常见问题见 **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)**。下面是最短路径。 ### 方式一：应用内安装（推荐） **设置 → 插件 → 安装**，在输入框里填 GitHub 短地址： ``` github:1015677515/dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk ``` 也可以填完整网址： ``` https://github.com/1015677515/dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk ``` 安装界面提示「输入插件的包名、GitHub 仓库地址或本地目录路径」，上面两种都是它接受的写法。 **不需要自己写 commit SHA。** 填不带版本后缀的短地址即可：市场会先把默认分支的 HEAD 解析成 40 位 commit SHA，再把 `github:owner/repo#` 这种已固定的形式交给 pnpm。这样 lockfile 里记录的是可追溯的提交，安装后**版本号能正常显示**。 > ⚠️ 反过来要注意：**不要**自己写 `#HEAD`，也不要让安装源停留在会移动的分支上。源码里写明，HEAD 形态的 tarball「installs perfectly and then reports no version forever」——能装上，但版本栏会一直是空的，之后也检测不到更新。 ### 方式二：本地目录 已经克隆到本地时，直接填目录路径（安装界面会提示「本地目录」）： ``` A:\大肥鱼工作区\dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk ``` 开发时这样最方便：local 安装默认以目录链接（Windows 上是 Junction）接入，改完源码刷新页面即可，不必重装。 ### 方式三：手动写进 profile ```yaml # cordis.patch.yml of your bundle - insert: - id: prompt-desk name: dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk ``` 装好后需要**重启 DSH**：浏览器半边会热重载，但宿主半边（负责往系统提示词注入）要重启才会加载新的模块代次。 ### 环境要求 | 依赖 | 要求 | |---|---| | DSH | `>=0.2.0-rc.1 || >=0.3.0-rc.1 || >=0.4.0-rc.1 || >=0.5.0-rc.1 || >=1.0.0-rc.1` | | Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` | | HTTP 服务 | 必需。宿主半边注册 `GET\|POST /prompt-desk/state`，浏览器半边靠它读写。没有 HTTP 服务的 profile 会加载插件但保持不活动，而不是报错 | 无第三方运行时依赖；浏览器半边只用页面已提供的 `react`，没有构建步骤。 ## 它会动你的哪些文件 全局提示词**就是** DSH 自己那个 `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md` —— 也就是官方 `dsh-agent-instructions` 插件本来就会读的同一个文件。本插件**不另存副本**：两个都自称「全局提示词」的文件必然会漂移，而且只有一个真正会送达模型。 | 数据 | 位置 | |---|---| | 全局提示词 | `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md` | | 本次对话提示词、错误库、面板开关 | `$DSH_HOME/prompt-desk/state.json` | 写入是**原子**的（先写 `.tmp` 再改名），崩溃不会截断你的提示词。浏览器半边完全不碰文件系统——所有读写都在宿主半边，所以不会写到 `$DSH_HOME` 之外。 ### 作者自用的提示词（仅供参考，不会被套用） 仓库根目录有一份 [`AGENTS.example.md`](AGENTS.example.md)，是插件作者自己正在用的全局提示词原文，公开出来纯粹当**写法参考**：你可以看看别人怎么分节组织、怎么把"先自检再交付""删除前报范围"这类要求写成一条能照着执行的话，然后照自己的习惯改。 **它不会覆盖你的提示词，装插件也不会。** 说清楚以免误会： - 安装插件不会写入你的 `AGENTS.md`。代码里唯一会写这个文件的地方是你在面板里点「保存」的那一刻，写的是**你自己输入框里的内容**，不是这个样例。 - 这个文件叫 `AGENTS.example.md`，不是 `AGENTS.md`，也没有放在会被自动加载的位置。DSH 的项目指令加载器只认 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `CLAUDE.local.md` 这几个**精确文件名**，`AGENTS.example.md` 不在名单里——哪怕你把这个仓库当工作区打开，它也不会被当成指令读进去。 - 没有"一键导入"按钮，这是有意为之：任何"帮你应用这份提示词"的功能，都是在覆盖你。 想用的话自己动手，最稳的方式是**先备份再合并**： ```powershell # DSH_HOME 没设置时插件用的是 ~/.dsh，这里跟着它走 $dsh = if ($env:DSH_HOME) { $env:DSH_HOME } else { Join-Path $HOME '.dsh' } Copy-Item "$dsh\AGENTS.md" "$dsh\AGENTS.md.bak" ``` 然后打开 `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`（也就是插件面板里的"全局提示词"框），挑你需要的那几条粘进去。直接整份覆盖也可以，但那会丢掉你原有的规则——**你的提示词应该长成你自己的样子，别人的只能当参考。** ## 注入是怎么工作的 本次对话提示词、以及**最近 10 条**错误经验，通过 `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` 注入，顺序值 `10200`（`DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_SUFFIX`），即排在工具文档之后。 - `text` 传的是**函数**，所以改完**下一轮对话就生效**——不用重启，也不用重新注册。 - 只注入**教训**。`detail` 解释了事情经过，`type` 是这次的事故标题——两者描述的都是**某一个瞬间**，只有碰上长得像的下一次任务才有用；而教训是一条能迁移的规则。`detail` 同时是 token 最贵的一项，所以两者都只留在面板里。 - **没有教训的条目不注入**，面板里会标出来让你补。它不占注入条数的额度——上限数的是"真正注入的条数"，所以先筛掉再取最近 N 条。 - 条数上限是为了不让经验库变成 token 黑洞：完整列表始终在面板里可读，提示词里也会说明当前只显示了其中一部分。 ### 注入条数可以自己设 **在错误库面板里直接填**（最方便）：面板里有一个「注入条数上限」输入框，填好点「保存」即可，下一轮对话生效。 | 字段 | 默认 | 含义 | |---|---|---| | `injectLimit` | `10` | 注入系统提示词的错误经验条数上限。`0` = 一条都不注入（会话提示词不受影响）；最大 `200`，填更大也会被夹到 200 | **优先级**：面板里填的值优先；清空输入框并保存（或点「恢复默认」）就回到"跟随插件配置"。 下面两种改法改的是**默认值**（面板没填时用它）： 1. **设置 → 插件 → 插件配置**（宿主从本插件的 `Config` schema 生成这个表单） 2. 写进 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`： ```yaml - id: prompt-desk name: dsh-prompt-ErrorNotes-desk config: injectLimit: 20 # 只接受非负整数 ``` 只接受**非负整数**：负数、小数、非数字会被拒绝（面板里会提示；schema 会给出具体原因，例如 `expected number >= 0 but got -5`）。 > 个别精简宿主可能不提供 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（设置表单由它生成）。那种情况下**功能不受影响**：面板里的输入框和 patch 的 `config` 都照常工作，只是设置里不会出现这个字段。 ## 错误经验库怎么分类 每一条都归到三个一级分类之一。面板按分类折叠展示，每条右侧的下拉框可以随时改类： | 一级分类 | 含义 | 二级分类 | |---|---|---| | 判断与依据错误 | 想错了 | 验证缺位（没核实就下结论）、依据缺位（凭推测代替取证） | | 生成与操作错误 | 做错了 | 语法生成（模板串、转义、拼接）、工具与编码（选错工具或破坏编码） | | 其他 | 暂未归类 | —（本身就是终点，不再细分） | 分类是**按补救手段**分的，不是按症状：每个二级分类都对应一个"下次换个做法"的具体动作，这样它才是可执行的，而不是描述性的。 - 老条目（v1 没有分类字段）会统一落在**其他**，在面板里用下拉框手工归档即可。插件**不会**按文本猜分类——猜错比不猜更糟。 - 分类 slug 写入时校验：手改状态文件写进一个不存在的分类，会被归到**其他**，不会污染面板。 ## 自动采集：agent 汇报「我犯了个错误」，它记下来 开启错误库导出时，插件会在系统提示词里附一段固定的**认错引导**（实际注入的全文，逐字）： ``` ## 自我认错 发现自身错误时，**必须**主动用下面这一行汇报： 我犯了个错误：错误经过：<当时实际发生了什么> 教训：<以后怎么做，一句可执行的规则> 两个标签缺一不可、顺序固定，且必须写在同一行；缺任一标签或换行都不会被捕获。分类由用户在面板里选。 错误经过 20 字以内，只写这次发生了什么；教训 40 字以内，但要写成换任务、换文件也成立的规则，不提本次的文件名、路径、命令或具体数值。 ``` 宿主半边监听助手的输出流，发现这个句式就把一条**草稿**放进面板顶部的「待确认」区，并在**错误库按钮上显示数字徽标**。草稿不会自动进库——必须点「采纳」；采纳前可以改措辞、选分类，或者直接「丢弃」。 - **两个标记都认**：`我犯了个错误`（引导里示范的那个）与 `我发现了个错误`。命中多个时，取**最靠前的、能解析成功的那一个**。 - **标记必须位于行首**（前面只允许空白、列表符号 `- * +`、有序列表序号或 `>`）。这一条是为了挡住"在句子里提到标记"——讨论本功能、引用代码、摘录文档时，标记常常出现在句子中间，那不是认错。 - **不合法的那一处会被跳过，而不是放弃整条消息**。这是很容易踩坑的一条：如果一条消息里**先提到**标记（引用它、演示格式、讨论本功能），**再写出真正的认错**，真正的认错**仍然会被捕获**——早先的实现只检查最靠前的那一个，一旦它在行中就整条放弃，结果是"边解释格式边认错"这种最常见的写法**静默丢失**。现在会继续往后找，直到找到合法的认错为止。 - **`错误经过：` 与 `教训：` 是硬边界**，且顺序固定、必须在同一行。这是取代旧 `｜` 分隔符的关键改动：分隔符太容易在散文里被引用（曾有一句话里写着"（忘了写 `｜`）"，结果在错误的位置切开，产生了垃圾草稿），而两个标签很难被无意复现。 - **必须写在同一行**：解析只看标记所在的那一行，所以「教训」换到下一行会**静默丢弃**——不会有任何报错，你也不会看到草稿。这是最容易踩的一条。 - **旧格式不再捕获**：`我犯了个错误：xxx｜yyy`（用 `｜` 分隔、无标签）不会再产生草稿，请用双标签格式。 - **20 / 40 字都是建议，不是硬限制**。代码只校验「错误经过」在 4~200 字之间；教训没有长度校验。写超了照样会被捕获，只是注入了 token 会多一些——面板里会把超过 40 字的教训标出来。 - **教训要写成可迁移的规则**。引导里明确要求"换任务、换文件也成立，不提本次的文件名、路径、命令或具体数值"，因为注入的是**教训**而不是事情经过：带具体文件名、具体命令的句子，只有下一次恰好同名时才用得上，而下一次几乎总是不同的文件。 - 一条消息**最多产生一条草稿**（取最先解析成功的那一处）；同一句话重复出现只算一次；队列上限 20 条，旧的先丢。 - 捕获到的内容若带尖括号（模型把模板本身回显出来）、以代码标点开头、或「错误经过」短于 4 字 / 长于 200 字，都会被**直接丢弃**——否则会记下"错误经过 = `<当时实际发生了什么>`"这类垃圾。 > 认错引导和错误经验列表由**同一个开关**控制：引导的存在就是为了喂这个库，库不注入时还留着引导，等于让 agent 对着空气认错。 ## 两个开关，位置刻意分开 有两个都会"停止注入错误经验"的开关。它们**作用范围不同**，所以放在提示词面板的**上下两端**，而不是挨在一起： | 开关 | 位置 | 停什么 | 是否持久 | |---|---|---|---| | 临时暂停注入（等同 `/lessons off`） | 面板**顶部** | 只停**错误经验列表**；本次对话提示词与「自我认错」引导照常生效 | 否，**重载后自动恢复为开启** | | 错误库导出到系统提示词 | 面板**底部** | 停**错误经验列表 + 自我认错引导** | 是，写进 `state.json` | 也可以在对话框里直接敲命令： ``` /lessons off 关闭（全局生效，跨对话） /lessons on 恢复 /lessons 不带参数则翻转当前状态 ``` > `/lessons` 是**全局**开关，且**重载后复位**——它的定位是"这一轮探索先别拿旧教训烦我"。要长期关掉，用面板底部的导出开关。参数写错会返回用法提示，不会静默翻转。 ## 你随时能看见"模型到底看到了什么" - **注入预览**：提示词面板里常驻一段等宽文本，就是插件对系统提示词的**完整贡献**，逐字发给模型。它和真实注入走**同一个构建函数**，所以两者不会各自漂移——这正是它存在的意义（只给一个"N 条"的统计数字，用户无法判断措辞对不对）。 - **安装自检**：提示词面板顶部一行状态，报告宿主半边是否加载、HTTP 路由是否可达、状态文件在哪、当前注入几条、有没有待确认、以及**界面与宿主的版本是否一致**。版本不一致时会提示刷新页面——界面 bundle 和宿主是从两个地方加载的，重建后其中一个常常领先一个版本。 ## 设计取舍 - What remains is what the parser *enforces* — both labels, their order, and the one-line rule (a confession split across two lines is dropped with no error, so omitting that rule would trade a silent failure for ~10 tokens). The error-list heading and its truncation note are Chinese now as well, which is about a third the length of the English for the same meaning. - **The cue asks for brevity**: incident and lesson should each stay within 20 characters. This is guidance, not enforcement — the parser still accepts an incident of 4–200 characters and places no bound on the lesson. It is kept in the cue despite being advice because a captured entry is re-injected on every later turn, so a shorter entry pays for itself many times over. - The category is still chosen in the panel rather than written into the line, and the cue says so, which answers "how do I fill in the library" at the point the model reads it. - The empty-state note in the panel and both READMEs were updated to the new format, and now show the injected cue verbatim. ## [0.4.0] — 2026-10-15 ### Added - **Categories.** Every entry now belongs to one of three top-level groups — `判断与依据错误` (with 验证缺位 / 依据缺位), `生成与操作错误` (with 语法生成 / 工具与编码) and `其他` — shown as collapsible groups with a per-row dropdown for re-filing. The split is by remedy, not symptom: each leaf names a concrete thing to do differently next time. `其他` is a declared, leaf-less group rather than a bucket the UI invents, so it flows through the same validation and the same dropdown as the other two. - **Automatic capture of self-reported mistakes.** The Host subscribes to `agent/assistant-stream`, accumulates the assistant's text deltas, and on a committed end runs the confession parser over the message. A recognized confession becomes a **draft** in the panel's 待确认 queue — never a library entry — with a count badge on the 错误库 header button. Drafts are editable (both the wording and the category) and can be accepted or discarded. - **The confession cue** (`我犯了个错误：<错在哪>｜<以后怎么避免>`) is now part of the injected text. It is what makes capture possible at all: free-form prose cannot be detected reliably. The fullwidth `｜` separator avoids colliding with markdown tables, code, or the arrows the lesson text already uses. - **Injection preview.** The prompt panel renders the plugin's entire contribution as a monospace block, produced by the same builder the assembler calls, so the preview cannot drift from what the model actually receives. - **Install self-check and a version handshake.** The panel reports Host liveness, the state-file location, the injected count, the pending count, and whether the bundle and the Host agree on `pluginVersion` — the last of which replaces the previous per-field defence against an older peer. - **`/lessons` command and a temporary-pause switch.** `/lessons off`, `/lessons on` or a bare `/lessons` (toggle) pauses the error list; the same control is a checkbox at the top of the prompt panel. It is **global** and **deliberately not persisted**. A mistyped argument returns usage rather than silently toggling. - **`GET /prompt-desk/pending`** — a deliberately trivial route so the header badge can poll a single integer instead of reading `AGENTS.md` and rebuilding the whole preview on every tick. ### Changed - **The panel's write protocol is addressed by entry id, not array index.** The Host now appends to the queue on its own, so an index the browser captured before that append would name a different entry. `errors` is no longer replaced wholesale: the patch carries `errorAdd` / `errorUpdate` / `errorDelete` / `pendingAccept` / `pendingDelete` / `pendingClear` / `lessonsEnabled`. - **State is v3.** A v1 (no ids, no categories) or v2 (`uncategorized` bucket) document is migrated by the first read that has to repair it, and the repaired file is written once. Migration is one-way; there is no downgrade path. - **Temporary files are now unique per write.** The atomic write used a fixed `${path}.tmp`, which was safe only while every write came from a user action. The Host writes on its own now, so two overlapping writers could have clobbered each other's bytes before the rename. - The prompt panel's two injection switches were moved to opposite ends of the panel. They overlap in effect but differ in scope, and sitting adjacent made them read as one control with two states. ### Notes - `/lessons` is global because no reliable mapping from `AssembleContext.scope` (an opaque `ScopeKey`) to `invocation.agent.id` was found in the installed harness. Guessing one would have produced a per-session switch that silently behaved globally anyway. - A listener registered on the plugin's global `ctx` **does** receive the `Scoped` `agent/assistant-stream` event. Verified at runtime in the desktop profile on 2026-10-15: a confession emitted in a real conversation was parsed into a pending draft (`source: "auto"`) in `state.json`. - The panel's write path is verified at runtime as well: accepting a captured draft and re-filing it to another category through the dropdown both persisted correctly to `state.json` — the promoted entry kept `source: "auto"` and was given a fresh unique id rather than reusing the draft's. The live `GET /prompt-desk/state` payload also carries the three-group tree, so the dropdown's five options are delivered by the Host, not invented by the bundle. - Still unverified at the time of writing: the `/lessons` command registration shape. It is isolated by `try`/`catch`, so a mismatch degrades to "command unavailable" rather than a failed plugin load. ## [0.3.0] — 2026-10-14 ### Added - **The cap is editable from the error-library panel.** A number field, a 保存 button and a 恢复默认 button sit inside the panel, next to the readout that says how many entries are actually reaching the model. The field's default and its bounds come from the Host, so it cannot drift from what the prompt assembler enforces, and it carries the reason to care: more entries means more tokens injected on every request. - **Clicking outside an open panel closes it**, and so does Escape. The listeners exist only while a panel is open, and the containment test covers both buttons and both panels, so pressing a button or typing in a field counts as inside. ### Changed - The cap now resolves per call from two sources, with one stated precedence: the panel's own value (stored in `state.json` as `injectLimit`) wins when set, and the plugin config's `injectLimit` is the default it falls back to. Clearing the panel field — or 恢复默认 — returns it to that default. - The panel payload gained `errorLimitDefault`, `errorLimitCustom` and `limitBounds`, so the Client renders the field's state from Host data instead of duplicating the rules. - The injection readout no longer points at Settings, since the setting is now in the panel it describes. ## [0.2.0] — 2026-10-14 ### Changed - **The injection cap now defaults to 10, down from 20.** The library exists so the model absorbs a reminder, and a list long enough to skim is a list that stops being read. Raise it again from the plugin config when the library is doing real work. ### Added - **`injectLimit` config field** — how many recent error entries reach the system prompt (`10` by default, `0` injects none, clamped to `200`). It is declared as the plugin's `Config` schema, so the host renders it under **Settings → Plugins → plugin config**, and it can equally be set from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`config.injectLimit`). A negative, fractional or non-numeric value is rejected by the schema with a specific reason. - The panel readout now prints the effective cap and where to change it, so the number on screen is one the user can act on. - `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` is declared as a peer dependency (`^3.18.1`). ## [0.1.0] — 2026-10-14 First release. ### Added - **Two panels in the conversation header** (`conversation.session.header.utilities`), mutually exclusive by construction: a single `openPanel` state means two panels cannot both be open. - **Prompt panel** — edits the cross-conversation global prompt (the harness's own `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`, so it is the same file the official `dsh-agent-instructions` plugin loads) and a per-session prompt that carries into the next conversation. Shows which half is currently reaching the model. - **Error library panel** — a dated list of recurring mistakes, each a short type plus a one-sentence lesson, with the original detail kept readable below it. - **System-prompt injection** — the session prompt and the most recent 20 error entries are contributed via `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` at `DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_SUFFIX` (10200). `text` is a function, so an edit takes effect on the next turn with no restart. - **Host-side persistence** — state lives in `$DSH_HOME/prompt-desk/state.json`, written atomically (`.tmp` sibling + rename). The browser half never touches the filesystem; it reads and writes through `GET|POST /prompt-desk/state`. ### Notes - The global prompt is deliberately **not** a private copy: two files both claiming to be "the global prompt" would drift, and only one of them would reach the model. - Panels use `--dsw-static-neutral-bluish-*` rather than `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-*`, so a liquid-glass theme plugin (which rewrites the aliases into translucent films) cannot make them see-through. MySQL connections and guarded database tools for DeepSeek Harness
Configure connections once, choose one or more per conversation, and let your agent route each call to a selected data source.

English | [中文](README.zh-CN.md) `dsh-mysql` is a profile bundle for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It adds a settings page for multiple MySQL connections, a per-session connection picker beside the composer, and four guarded tools that every agent preset can use. No preset edits are required. > **Data boundary:** connection settings and passwords stay in your local DSH storage. Database schema and query results are sent to the LLM provider as ordinary tool output when the agent uses a database tool. ## At a glance | Surface | What it provides | | --- | --- | | **Settings → MySQL 数据库** | Add, edit, delete, and test connections. Configure host, port, user, password, default database, table scope, row-write permission, and independent schema-change permission. | | **Composer database button** | Select or deselect one or more data sources for the current session. Each click takes effect immediately; the composer pill shows the single name or a compact selected count. | | **Agent tools + runtime context** | `mysql_tables`, `mysql_query`, `mysql_execute`, and `mysql_ddl`, plus a per-turn context snapshot listing this session's selected sources and capabilities. | ## Features - **Multiple connections:** keep separate development, staging, or production data sources in one DSH installation. - **Per-session multi-selection:** each conversation independently selects zero, one, or multiple sources. Select/deselect takes effect immediately; clearing the last selection leaves the session without database access until a source is selected again. A session with multiple configured sources starts empty; a sole configured source is auto-selected on first initialization. Selection is runtime-only and is not restored after a DSH restart. - **One target per tool call:** when multiple sources are selected, the agent passes one selected `connectionId` to each tool call. A single selected source may be inferred. Queries are never broadcast or merged across sources. - **Schema-first workflow:** `mysql_tables` exposes readable columns, types, nullability, keys, and comments before a query is written. - **Read-only by default:** row-write access and schema-change access are independent per-connection settings, both disabled by default and each requiring its own risk acknowledgement. - **Scoped schema changes:** `mysql_ddl` is separate from `mysql_execute`; changed/deleted targets are checked against the table allowlist, and explicit database qualifiers must match the connection's default database. Account/privilege and database-level statements remain refused. - **Local-first configuration:** the browser receives a safe connection view with `hasPassword`, never the stored password. - **No preset changes:** the tools are registered globally by the profile bundle and are available under every agent preset. ## Agent tools | Tool | Accepted input and behavior | | --- | --- | | `mysql_tables` | Lists columns from one selected database through `information_schema`. Pass `connectionId` when multiple sources are selected; it may be omitted when exactly one is selected. Optional `table` filtering is case-insensitive. Results respect that source's table allowlist. | | `mysql_query` | Executes one read-only `SELECT`, `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`/`DESC`, or `EXPLAIN` statement against one selected source. Pass `connectionId` when multiple sources are selected; it may be omitted for a single selection. Optional `?` parameters are supported. It rejects multi-statement SQL, applies the target source's table-scope check, and returns up to 2,000 serialized rows with a `truncated` flag. | | `mysql_execute` | Executes one `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` statement against one selected source. Pass `connectionId` when multiple sources are selected; it may be omitted for a single selection. Requires that target's `allowWrite: true`; DDL, transaction-control statements, multi-statement SQL, and other statement types are rejected. | | `mysql_ddl` | Executes one `CREATE`/`ALTER`/`DROP`/`RENAME`/`TRUNCATE` statement on tables, views, or indexes in one selected source. Pass `connectionId` when multiple sources are selected; it may be omitted for a single selection. It requires that target's independent `allowDdl: true` setting; changed/deleted targets obey its allowlist and all explicit database qualifiers must match its default database. Account/privilege statements and database-level DDL are always rejected. | Schema changes require a separate opt-in and risk acknowledgement. Once enabled, you can ask the agent to create a table, for example: ```text Inspect the current schema with mysql_tables, then create `agent_notes` in this connection's default database with an auto-increment id, title, and created_at timestamp. Show the CREATE TABLE SQL and execute it with mysql_ddl. Do not modify other tables. ``` If the connection has a non-empty table allowlist, add the new table to that list before asking the agent to read or write it with the existing tools. A typical read-only request is: ```text Use mysql_tables to inspect the available schema first, then use mysql_query to answer my question. Do not modify data. ``` ### Multi-source routing example When a conversation has more than one selected source, route every database call explicitly: ```text Inspect both selected sources separately. For each source, call mysql_tables and then run: SELECT @@port AS server_port, DATABASE() AS database_name, VERSION() AS server_version Pass exactly one selected connectionId per call, label every result with its source, and do not merge or broadcast results. ``` The picker changes the session's selected set immediately. A session with multiple configured sources starts empty, a sole configured source is auto-selected on first initialization, and clearing the final source leaves the session explicitly empty until the user selects a source again. Selection is kept in memory and is not restored after a DSH restart. ## Requirements and compatibility - A DSH installation with the **Web profile** and Node.js **20 or newer**. - **DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer, below 0.3.0.** Version 0.2.0 of this plugin migrates its Typert RPC manifest to the DSH 0.2 strict codec contract (`create()` factory) and no longer loads on DSH 0.1.x — use plugin 0.1.11 there. - A MySQL-compatible server reachable through the configured TCP host and port. - The connection form currently supports host, port, username, password, default database, table allowlist, and write permission. It does not expose SSL/TLS, Unix socket/named-pipe, or charset options. - The `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` optimizer hint is intended for MySQL versions that support it (MySQL 5.7.8+). MariaDB may handle this hint differently; `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`, and `EXPLAIN` do not receive the hint. - `mysql_tables` discovers tables in `DATABASE()`. Configure a default database if you want schema discovery; a connection without one can return an empty table list. ## Install, update, or remove ### Install from GitHub ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web add github:1321928757/dsh-mysql#v0.3.1 ``` ### Install from npm Use this after `dsh-mysql` is available in the npm registry: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mysql ``` ### PowerShell installer The repository also provides a Windows installer that checks for `dsh`, prepares a pinned pnpm helper under `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh-tmp`, and installs the selected GitHub tag into the `web` profile: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/v0.3.0/scripts/install.ps1 | iex ``` After installation, restart `dsh web`. Then open **Settings → MySQL 数据库**, add and test one or more connections, and select them from the database button beside the composer. Verify that the bundle is in the profile: ```powershell dsh --profile web --dump-config | findstr dsh-mysql ``` Remove it with: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-mysql ```
Update or install from a local checkout Update the installed package from GitHub: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-mysql@latest ``` For local development, install the checkout or a packed tarball into a separate profile first: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile demo add E:\path\to\dsh-mysql dsh --profile demo --dump-config ```
## Quick start 1. Open **Settings → MySQL 数据库** and click **添加连接**. Fill in the host, port, username, password, and default database. Optionally add readable table names and enable write permission only when needed. Test the connection, then save it. 2. Open a conversation and click the database button on the left of the composer. Select or deselect one or more connections for that session; each click takes effect immediately and the picker stays open. If exactly one connection is configured, it is selected automatically when the session first initializes. With multiple selections, the agent chooses a target per tool call by `connectionId`; deselecting every source disables database tools for that session. Selection is not persisted across a DSH restart. 3. Ask a database question. The agent can inspect the schema with `mysql_tables`, read with `mysql_query`, use `mysql_execute` only for an explicitly writable connection, or use `mysql_ddl` only when the separate schema-change permission is enabled. ## Screenshots The screenshots below were captured from the real DSH Web shell with the plugin loaded. Connection names and account names in the settings example are illustrative; passwords are not shown. ### Configure a connection The settings page groups connection details, database scope, and permissions. Read-only is the default. The add-connection form keeps **保存连接** as the primary action, while **测试连接** remains a quieter secondary action. ![MySQL settings page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/main/assets/settings.png) The form can be opened below the saved connection cards without leaving the settings page: ![Add MySQL connection form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/main/assets/settings-add-form.png) ### Select data sources for a session The composer shows the database control even before a connection is selected. Its arrow points down while the picker is closed: ![Composer without a selected database connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/main/assets/conversation-no-connection.png) Click it to search and choose from the configured connections. The arrow points up while the list is expanded: ![Per-session database connection picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/main/assets/conversation-picker.png) After one connection is selected, its name, green status dot, and down arrow appear in the composer. With multiple selections, the compact composer pill shows the selected count instead of stacking connection-name chips. The picker uses the existing card layout and selected-row treatment; each change applies immediately. The selected sources and their individual capabilities are included in the conversation context shown to the agent: ![Selected connection in conversation context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/main/assets/conversation-context.png) After the agent runs a read-only query, the tool result is displayed in the conversation: ![MySQL query result](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1321928757/dsh-mysql/main/assets/conversation-query.png) ## Security and permissions The plugin uses multiple guardrails, but it does not replace database permissions. Use a dedicated MySQL account with the least privileges possible; for read-only work, a `SELECT`-only account is recommended. | Guardrail | What is enforced | Important boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Statement type | `mysql_query` accepts read statements; `mysql_execute` accepts only `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`; `mysql_ddl` accepts the supported table/view/index schema changes. | The tool layer is not a general SQL console. | | Row-write permission | `mysql_execute` requires the selected connection's `allowWrite` flag. | Per connection, default off, with a separate risk acknowledgement. | | Schema-change permission | `mysql_ddl` requires the independent `allowDdl` flag; changed/deleted targets obey the allowlist, and explicit database qualifiers must match the default database. | Default off with a separate acknowledgement; account/privilege and database-level statements stay refused. | | Multi-statement SQL | Multiple statements and transaction/control statements are rejected. | Schema changes are issued one statement per call. | | Table allowlist | Checks table references detected after `FROM`, `JOIN`, `UPDATE`, and `INTO`. An empty list means no configured table restriction. | This is a lexical check, not a full SQL parser. Forms such as `DESCRIBE t` or `SHOW CREATE TABLE t` do not use those reference keywords; combine the allowlist with database-level grants. | | Result size | The serialized tool response contains at most 2,000 rows and reports `truncated: true` when rows were omitted. | The query is fetched before the response is truncated; this is not a server-side scan or network limit. | | Credential exposure | Passwords are stored in local `connections.json`; the browser receives only `hasPassword`. | Query results, schema, and tool arguments are still sent to the configured LLM provider. | Passwords are stored as plain text in `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-mysql/connections.json`. Protect this file with operating-system permissions and do not commit or share it. ## Known limitations - Each conversation session independently selects zero, one, or multiple database sources; changes do not affect other sessions. An empty selection disables database tools for that session. Selection state is kept in memory and reinitialized after a DSH restart. - Each tool call targets exactly one source; when multiple sources are selected, `connectionId` is required. The plugin does not broadcast queries or merge results across databases. - `mysql_tables` uses the connection's `DATABASE()` value, so schema discovery may be empty when no default database is configured. It does not browse arbitrary databases. - The table allowlist is intentionally lightweight and checks common table-reference positions rather than parsing every MySQL grammar form. - The 2,000-row limit applies to the returned JSON payload after the database response has been fetched. - `mysql_execute` remains limited to row writes; it does not provide transaction management or a confirmation workflow. `mysql_ddl` has no per-call approval; it is guarded by a per-connection opt-in, allowlist, and default-database boundary. Use a narrowly scoped database account. - Connection configuration is TCP-oriented and has no UI for SSL/TLS, Unix sockets/named pipes, or character-set selection. ## How it works ```text Composer / Settings UI │ browser slot + Typert RPC (remote.mysql.*) ▼ Host mysql service │ per-session selection + lazy mysql2 pool ├── local JSON: $DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-mysql/connections.json └── systemPrompt.context: selected sources + per-source scopes/capabilities ``` - **Host bundle (`lib/index.js`)** registers the four model tools, manages lazy mysql2 pools, persists connections, tracks each session's selected source set, and provides the `mysql` service. Every resolved tool result includes the selected source name and `connectionId`; a resolved error is prefixed the same way without exposing credentials. - **Typert manifest (`lib/typert.host.js`)** exposes connection CRUD, testing, selection, and table-list methods to the browser through `remote.mysql.*`. - **Browser bundle (`lib/client.js`)** registers the `conversation.input.left` database control and the `settings.section` connection-management page. UI styles consume DSH `--dsw-*` theme tokens. - The selected sources are added through `systemPrompt.context` as a dynamic tail section, so changing the selection set does not rewrite the stable cached system-prompt prefix. When multiple sources are selected, the context instructs the model to pass exactly one selected `connectionId` per tool call. ## Migrating from a preset-embedded MySQL tool If a preset previously embedded `mysql_query` or `mysql_execute` through a local tool row: 1. Install this plugin into the profile. 2. Remove the old MySQL tool row and connection configuration from the preset's `agent.cordis.yml`; keep the business persona text. 3. Restart `dsh web`, then recreate the connection in **Settings → MySQL 数据库**. The tool names are unchanged, so prompts that mention them continue to work. ## FAQ and troubleshooting
The database button is missing Restart the DSH Web process after installation or update. Then verify the profile composition with `dsh --profile web --dump-config | findstr dsh-mysql`. Make sure the plugin was installed into the same profile that you started.
“No MySQL connection is configured” or “this session has not selected a connection” Open **Settings → MySQL 数据库** and save at least one connection. In the conversation, click the database button and select one or more sources for this session. A single saved source is auto-selected when the session first initializes; multiple configured sources start with none selected. If you have cleared all selections, select a source again to restore tool access.
Connection tests fail Check the host and port, credentials, default database, server reachability, and the MySQL account's network permissions. The plugin connects from the DSH host, not from the browser. For startup diagnostics, inspect `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-mysql/boot.log`.
The table list is empty Set a default database in the connection form. `mysql_tables` queries `information_schema.columns` for `table_schema = DATABASE()` and will not enumerate another schema automatically.
A write, DDL, multi-statement, or allowlist query was rejected Use `mysql_query` for one read statement and `mysql_execute` only for one `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` when `allowWrite` is enabled. To change schema, enable the independent `allowDdl` permission with its acknowledgement and use `mysql_ddl`; it accepts only table/view/index CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, or TRUNCATE in the default database. Account/privilege statements, database-level DDL, transaction/control statements, multiple statements, and references outside the configured table scope remain blocked. The allowlist is a lexical check; database-level grants remain the final boundary.
Does the browser receive my password? No. The browser receives a safe connection view containing `hasPassword`, not the password value. The local JSON file still stores the password in plain text, so protect that file.

Optimization uses the provider and model selected by DSH. When context is enabled, the request may include recent messages, the current goal and todo list, a compaction summary, and optional tool-result summaries. The draft and enabled context are therefore visible to that model provider; review its privacy and retention policy before using the feature with sensitive conversations. ## At a glance | Surface | What it provides | | --- | --- | | **Composer → Optimize** | Rewrite the current draft, show the result for review, or stop an in-flight optimization. | | **Composer → gear** | Quick settings for context, tool summaries, mode, and language; opens the full settings dialog. | | **DSH Settings → General** | A linked `settings.general.item` row for the **Reference conversation context** switch. An explicit language choice is applied after optional custom preferences; in Translate and optimize mode, **Follow draft** means optimize without translating. - Optional context injection from the current session: goal, todo list, compaction summary, recent messages, and—when both context switches are enabled—short tool-result summaries. - A result popover with the original draft, optimized draft, **Adopt optimized result**, **Keep draft**, and **Later** actions. Results are never automatically adopted. - Stop while a model stream is running; when the DSH conversation-block API is available, clear the composer block immediately and ignore late results from the cancelled run. - Failure results stay visible with the original draft and a **Retry** action. - A current-component, in-memory history of the last five optimization attempts. The optimizer instructs the model to output one user-facing request rather than an answer, plan, explanation, or code fence. This is a model instruction, not a deterministic output filter: review the generated text before adopting it. ## Runtime behavior and limits This plugin is a browser composer extension, not a standalone shell command or a model tool exposed to the agent. The browser calls the Host `promptPolish` service through Typert RPC; the Host then streams a request through DSH's configured LLM service. | Area | Implemented behavior | | --- | --- | | Draft validation | Empty or whitespace-only drafts are rejected. Drafts longer than **20,000 characters** are rejected. | | Context collection | Opt-in. The browser scans up to **20 message nodes** and up to **8,000 rolling message characters**. A message over 4,000 characters is reduced to its first 2,600 and last 1,400 characters. | | Goal, todo, and compaction | The current goal and todo list are placed before message turns when available. At most the last three tool calls in a selected assistant turn are summarized, with the first 300 characters of each result. | | Host-side context budget | The Host keeps at most 30 message items and 60 tool-summary items from the payload, then prunes items again to fit the selected model's context budget. Some context can therefore be omitted. | | Stream timeouts | **30 seconds** without a new chunk, or **120 seconds** total. Either timeout returns an error that can be retried. | | Output budget | The request is capped at **4,000 output tokens**, also limited by the selected model and remaining context. The requested floor is 1,200 tokens; a model reaching its limit can return a result marked as possibly truncated. | | Cancellation | Each run receives a `runId`. Stop calls `cancelOptimize`, aborts the Host stream, and discards a late result. | | Adoption guard | Adoption requires an explicit button click and succeeds only if the composer draft is still exactly the draft that was optimized. Type a draft into the DSH composer. 2. Optionally open the gear and enable **Reference conversation context**. Enable **Include tool results** only if you also want the context request to include short tool summaries. 3. Choose a mode and language. In **Translate and optimize**, the language selector is the target language. 4. Open **Full settings** if you need a custom instruction of up to 500 characters, or want to inspect the context preview and recent attempt history. 5. Click **Optimize**. The composer is blocked while the request is running when the conversation block API is available; the button becomes **Stop optimizing**. 6. Inspect the original and generated prompt in the result popover. 7. Choose **Adopt optimized result**, **Keep draft**, or **Later**. The latter two only dismiss the result; they do not save a reminder. A changed draft cannot be overwritten by an older result. The **Retry** action reuses the original snapshot from the failed attempt. The **Refill** action in history is an explicit write to the composer and is different from automatic adoption. ## Screenshots The screenshots use published GitHub Raw URLs so they render in GitHub, npm, and external marketplace views after the repository assets are pushed. ### Composer entry The **Optimize** button and gear are registered in the composer's `conversation.input.left` slot.
